title: kb_backlog usage returns a backlog.py verb's arguments, so a session reads them without 436 --help runs
goal: kb_backlog usage with no argument returns the verb list with one line each, and usage gate add returns gate add's argument list with --recommendation; usage writes no file and runs no item

run:
import sys
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kb_mcp
def call(a):
 try:return str(kb_mcp.kb_backlog({"command":"usage","args":a}))
 except Exception as e:return "ERR "+str(e)[:150]
a=call(["gate","add"]);b=call([])
print(a[:120],"|",b[:120])
sys.exit(0 if "--recommendation" in a and "dispatch" in b and not b.startswith("ERR") else 1)

import hashlib,subprocess as s,sys
sys.path.insert(0,"_tools");import kb_mcp
def call(a):
 try:return str(kb_mcp.kb_backlog({"command":"usage","args":a}))
 except Exception as e:return "ERR "+str(e)[:150]
f="kb/_self/backlog/ST-uruhigy4.json"
st=lambda:(hashlib.sha256(open(f,"rb").read()).hexdigest(),s.run(["git","status","--porcelain"],capture_output=True,text=True).stdout)
a=st();v=call([]);outs=[call(["claim","ST-uruhigy4"]),call(["done","ST-uruhigy4"]),call(["dispatch"])];b=st()

notes: From the 2026-10-24 telemetry and query-log analysis: backlog.py --help or SUBCOMMAND --help ran 436 times in 121 sessions in 7 days (149k tokens of help text, average 1.36k characters, 28 in one session): new 94, set 87, close 53, gate 53, start 21, dispatch 19, tidy 19, answer 18; managers 398, workers 38. All tools together 615 calls in 149 sessions. kbgit.py publish --help is denied by a Bash rule (4 calls) and has no other route; kb_backlog refuses 'set --help' today because set is not in its list. Same argparse text, no new information: it saves the Bash round trip and the first-try mistakes they precede. Near ST-pntfa6ry (usage text of a changed verb).
